benchmark_gaps: No performance benchmarks for sensor placement at scale (10k+ sensors/targets); _greedy is O(S*T) per pass and _greedy_indexed still has O(S*T) selection loop with no lazy-greedy priority-queue optimization
No benchmarks for device registry operations at scale (10k+ devices); all operations are O(N) linear scans with no indexing beyond dict lookup
No benchmarks for MQTT publish/subscribe throughput or Kafka produce/consume latency under load
No benchmarks for TimescaleDB query performance with large datasets; in-memory list scans are O(N) per query
No benchmarks for anomaly detection throughput (IQR/EWMA/Welford) on high-frequency sensor streams
No benchmarks for consistent hash ring rebalancing cost when nodes are added/removed
No benchmarks for LoRaWAN air-time calculation or duty-cycle enforcement at scale
No benchmarks for spatial index (k-d tree) construction and query performance vs brute-force baseline
No benchmarks for data validation pipeline throughput (schema + range + cross-field + temporal + rate-of-change)
No benchmarks for NGSI-LD context broker entity CRUD latency or subscription notification throughput
bottlenecks: Sensor placement greedy selection is O(S*T) per iteration; no lazy greedy (priority queue) or submodular optimization for large deployments
Device registry uses in-memory dict with no persistence, no indexing by status/type, and O(N) scans for list_devices and get_offline_devices
MQTT client is synchronous with no async I/O; publish blocks on all subscriber callbacks sequentially
Kafka stream uses in-memory queue.Queue with no backpressure propagation, no partition rebalancing, and no consumer group coordination
TimescaleDB storage uses in-memory list with O(N) scans for every query; no indexing, no batch inserts, no connection pooling
Data validation pipeline runs all validators sequentially with no short-circuit or parallel evaluation
Anomaly detectors (IQR/EWMA) recompute statistics from scratch on every update; no incremental optimization for high-frequency streams
Consistent hash ring rebuilds entire ring on node add/remove; no incremental update
LoRaWAN simulator is single-threaded with no concurrent device support
Context broker client is synchronous with no connection pooling, no retry logic, and no circuit breaker
Device shadow has no sync protocol; desired/reported state reconciliation is manual with no conflict resolution
No edge computing layer; all data flows to cloud with no local preprocessing, filtering, or aggregation
No data lineage tracking; cannot trace a reading from sensor through pipeline to storage
No TLS/mTLS support anywhere in the IoT stack; all connections are plaintext
MQTT QoS parameter is accepted but ignored; all messages are delivered as QoS 0 (fire-and-forget)
missing_algorithms: Edge computing: no local data processing, filtering, aggregation, or rule engine at the edge
Edge computing: no edge-to-cloud sync protocol with conflict resolution and offline buffering
Digital twin sync: no bidirectional sync protocol between physical devices and digital twins
Digital twin sync: no conflict resolution strategy for concurrent desired/reported state updates
Digital twin sync: no twin-to-physical reconciliation loop with convergence guarantees
MQTT QoS 1: no at-least-once delivery with PUBACK tracking and retry logic
MQTT QoS 2: no exactly-once delivery with PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP handshake
TLS: no TLS 1.2/1.3 support for MQTT, CoAP (DTLS), or HTTP connections
TLS: no certificate management, rotation, or mTLS for device authentication
Data lineage: no provenance tracking from sensor reading through transformations to storage
Data lineage: no audit trail for data modifications or pipeline stage transitions
Sensor placement: no weighted Set Cover (sensor cost/energy/reliability)
Sensor placement: no multi-objective optimization (coverage vs cost vs redundancy)
Sensor placement: no terrain-aware or obstacle-aware placement (signal propagation models)
Sensor placement: no incremental placement for dynamic target sets
Device management: no bulk provisioning or decommissioning workflows
Device management: no device grouping/hierarchy (field -> zone -> farm)
Device management: no certificate-based device authentication (X.509)
Device management: no secure boot or firmware signature verification
Data pipeline: no windowing (tumbling, sliding, session) for stream processing
Data pipeline: no watermarking for out-of-order event processing
Data pipeline: no exactly-once semantics across pipeline stages
Data pipeline: no data compression or delta encoding for bandwidth-constrained links
Anomaly detection: no seasonal decomposition or STL for agricultural time series
Anomaly detection: no multivariate anomaly detection (correlated sensor failures)
Anomaly detection: no online clustering for anomaly pattern discovery
LoRaWAN: no downlink scheduling optimization or multicast
LoRaWAN: no interference modeling or channel allocation
Consistent hashing: no bounded-load variant for hot-key mitigation
No circuit breaker pattern for failing downstream services
No rate limiting or backpressure propagation across pipeline stages
No async/await support for I/O-bound operations (MQTT, Kafka, TimescaleDB, NGSI-LD)
